digest.component_or_area: rebar reconciler: Jira-family adapter layer and ADR governance
propositions: ADR 0035 must be amended to document the jira_family two-level seam architecture, not replaced wholesale, recording the parameterizing contracts and shared-jira provenance decision with explicit deferral of generalizing the vocabulary to epic be74.

The TicketTransport protocol declares six members but the core reconciler reaches for twenty-one distinct members; twelve are absent from the DC transport and undeclared on any Protocol, causing silent failures until a live crash occurs while isinstance, contract suite, and 1636 unit tests all pass green.

ADR 0035 contains four stale statements across three locations (diagram comment at :111, prose at :204-205, Decision item 6 at :236-237, Consequences section) falsely claiming the first real second backend is out of scope, when epic e369 landed Jira Data Center ahead of the GitHub adapter be74.

RemoteRef.instance is never constructed in production code (only in two test helpers), so the shared-jira provenance decision must be documented as intended design with the implementation gap named and tracked, not asserted as existing reality.

The ADR must state plainly that ADR 0035's claim 'the contract suite certifies a backend' is conditional on the port being complete and typed, citing evidence that an unannotated client parameter makes port-incompleteness gaps invisible to mypy.

The March 2029 Data Center read-only date and non-existence of official DC OpenAPI specs establish this as a deliberately time-boxed investment for self-hosted clients, with the durable asset being the family seam rather than the DC adapter, informing future investment decisions.
